question: ttft
answer:
Time measurement happens in `stream_chat()` (`src/nvidia_ai/llm.py:104-193`): it opens an SSE POST to `/chat/completions` with `t0 = clock()` at request start, then for each streamed chunk computes `now = clock() - t0` whenever a delta carries content or reasoning. It sets `result.ttft_s` on the first such delta and keeps updating `result.last_token_s` on every subsequent one; `result.total_s` is set to `clock() - t0` once the stream finishes (or fails).

Rate calculation is done via two properties on `ChatResult` (`src/nvidia_ai/llm.py:73-94`):
- `.decode_tps()` (L73-87) — `completion_tokens / (last_token_s - ttft_s)`, i.e. tokens generated after the first token, excluding TTFT. Suppressed below `MIN_TOKENS_FOR_TPS`/`MIN_GEN_TIME_S` to avoid noise from short answers.
- `.e2e_tps()` (L89-94) — `completion_tokens / total_s`, i.e. end-to-end throughput including TTFT.

The benchmark driver (`src/nvidia_ai/bench.py`) calls `stream_chat()` from `run()` (L141) and `_with_retries()` (L111), records each `ChatResult` via `_record()` (L205), which reads `.decode_tps` and `.e2e_tps` off it (L223-224), and aggregates medians in `summarize()`/`_median()` (L238, L233) for the final report (`to_markdown()`, L283).
